problems.question: Manganese has seven electrons outside its argon core. How are they arranged at the lowest energy?

options.label: 4s² 3d⁵, each 3d electron alone in its own orbital

problems.explanation: 4s fills first in the neutral atom, then 3d takes one electron per orbital: five 3d electrons fill all five orbitals singly, with no pair.

problems.question: Nickel's outer electrons are 4s² 3d⁸. Which arrangement does the Ni²⁺ ion have?
problems.explanation: Once the atom carries a charge its 3d level lies below 4s, so the two 4s electrons leave first and Ni²⁺ keeps all eight 3d electrons.

problems.question: Magnesium's first three ionization energies are 738, 1451 and 7733 kJ/mol. Which ion does magnesium form?
problems.explanation: The cost jumps more than fivefold at the third electron, which would come from the full inner shell, so magnesium loses two electrons and forms Mg²⁺.

problems.question: Scandium forms only the Sc³⁺ ion, and its outer electrons are 4s² 3d¹. Is scandium a transition metal by the definition used on this bench?

options.label: No: Sc³⁺ has no 3d electrons left
Yes: its atom has a 3d electron
Yes: it forms an ion with a charge of 3+
No: it is not in the fourth row

problems.explanation: Sc³⁺ has lost all three outer electrons, so its 3d subshell is empty. On this bench a transition metal must form an ion with a partly filled 3d subshell. Some books also count elements whose atoms have a partly filled d subshell, and by that rule scandium counts.
